clips.title: Rockstar hired a real cartel smuggler to research GTA 6
clips.hook: Their contact hooked them up with a smuggler who knew Pablo Escobar.
clips.description: To get Vice City right, Rockstar's researcher sat down with a man who built submarines for Colombian cartels in the 70s - the same consultant they used for the Cayo Perico heist. He'd been kidnapped by the cartel himself.
clips.why: The strongest story in the video and the only one that is genuinely surprising. Self-contained, has a concrete image (drug submarines) and a dark payoff that lands inside a minute.

clips.title: You can read a GTA 6 code through the case with a flashlight
clips.hook: There's an even easier way to get GTA 6 for free.
clips.description: Whoever printed the physical cases embedded the code in the back of the case instead of on a card. Shine a light through the plastic, write down the code, return the box. Some buyers are already receiving cases with codes that have been used.
clips.why: The most shareable thing in the video: a real exploit, explained in one sentence, with a twist ending that makes it news rather than a tip.

sfx_cues.reason: the turn: boxes arriving with no code at all

clips.title: GTA 6 made $1.5 billion before anyone played it
clips.hook: Pre-order numbers beating GTA 5 and Cyberpunk combined.
clips.description: Sensor Tower estimates 14.94 million copies pre-sold, about $1.5 billion, three quarters of it on PlayStation 5 - enough to cover most of the development budget before launch day.
clips.why: Numbers travel. Three concrete figures in under a minute, each bigger than the last, ending on the $2 billion launch-week projection.
